svg.aria-label: YARA ruleset build pipeline: rule sources and config feed a fourteen-stage build with six hard gates, a filter engine with three cross-checks, and CI stages producing dist artifacts and a tagged release.
svg.title: YARA ruleset build pipeline
svg.desc: Full data flow for scripts/build_ruleset.py, including lint, the filter engine, and the GitLab CI stages.
svg.text: Full data flow — sources and config in, fourteen build stages and their gates in the middle, dist/ artifacts and a tagged release out. Source: docs/build_pipeline.mmd
A gate's pass path is the vertical spine; its failure paths branch to the right.

g.text: sorted glob · committed as received (exempt from required_meta)
single fixed path · replaces named vendor rules
required_meta · meta_dates · the two decision-file paths
a rule: scope or match.name not in the corpus
0 · Load config, override manifest, filter policy
config_schema.load_* — any ConfigError (missing file, unknown key, bad enum) blocks
config/build.yaml: output_formats — every entry must be "source"
identifier · meta · tags · condition_terms · imports · origin · filepath
a plyara parse failure blocks: "failed to parse <path>"
manifest semantics + every supersedes target must still exist in vendor
run pre-filter on purpose — a duplicate id is a source defect
config/build.yaml: yara_modules — pe, elf, math (D-1, Corelight Fleet Manager)
config/build.yaml: meta_dates — fields, input_formats, on_unparsable · every origin
BLOCK — a non-source format is configured
D-2: Corelight compiles internally; .yarc is never emitted
BLOCK — stale override, no recorded decision
the error prints a paste-ready YAML entry
warn — decision: discard · keep passes silently
logs "REQUIRED CLEANUP"; a returned vendor rule also warns
the compile gate cannot catch it — yara-python supports more modules
every offender is logged and removed from the corpus; the drops become

svg.text: 8 · FILTER POLICY — scripts/apply_filters.py · a selection layer, it never edits or deletes source rules

g.text: the stage-7 date drops enter here, so they face all three cross-checks and reach the manifest
selector keys AND together: name · name_glob · name_regex · tags · meta · meta_in · meta_date
no filter applies → default_mode from filter_policy.yaml (include_all — a denylist, D-9)
Conflict at the same specificity → EXCLUDE WINS
D-8, hardcoded — any other tie-break makes output depend on filter order, or blocks on a resolvable conflict
the merged source would not compile
the exclusion record becomes filtered_rules in the build manifest — one entry per rule, with the filter id that excluded it
◆ 9 · topological_order — a referenced rule must precede its referrer
Kahn's algorithm on a min-heap keyed (GROUP_ORDER, input_position, identifier)
default emission order vendor 0 → overrides 1 → custom 2 · deterministic (NFR-6)
nothing has been written to disk yet
runs against the in-memory source, before anything reaches dist/
reached only once the compile has passed
records what was removed, what was filtered, and the hash of every input
attributed to a specific rule by a bisect over rule_index (_locate_rule)
no artifact is emitted — dist/ is never touched

svg.text: BUILD ARTIFACTS — dist/ (gitignored locally, passed to the test stage as a CI artifact)

g.text: a single compilation unit, deterministic order (NFR-6)
sorted import lines, then vendor → overrides → custom

svg.text: CI STAGE: image — only when its inputs change

g.text: rules: changes to ci/Dockerfile or requirements.txt
validates the built dist/ artifacts; it never rebuilds inline
→ test-results/ + junit.xml (when: always, surfaced in the MR)
deferred pending D-3; a manual job over an uploaded PCAP
package · tag only — needs: build, test
curl image (the CI image is -slim and ships no curl)
a red test suite therefore blocks the release
release-cli get probe first, then create — idempotent when
the Release already exists (UI-created tag, or a retried pipeline)
tied to its exact inputs by source_hashes + build_version
